title: The tannaim
hook: the sages of the Mishnah, from Hillel's time to Rabbi Judah the Prince

segments.voice: Yesterday, why it was written down: a terse text, made to go back into the mouth. Your line: write it before it's lost. Today, the people whose words were saved.

Open the Mishnah almost anywhere and you hear a room full of people. Rabbi Meir says this. Rabbi Judah says that. Rabbi Shimon disagrees, and the sages say something else. The house of Shammai, the house of Hillel. Rabban Gamaliel, Rabbi Akiva, Rabbi Eliezer. It reads less like a rulebook than the minutes of a very long meeting, with everyone's name attached to what they said. The Talmud has a single word for each of these teachers, and it's today's word.
screen: `RABBI MEIR SAYS. RABBI JUDAH SAYS.` → `A ROOM FULL OF NAMES.` → `ONE WORD FOR EACH OF THEM.`

segments.voice: Tanna. In the plural, tannaim. It's an Aramaic word, and Jastrow's dictionary of Talmudic Aramaic ties it to repeating, and so to teaching, because this teaching was learned by saying it over and over. The tannaim are the sages of the Mishnah, from Hillel and Shammai down to Rabbi Judah the Prince, who gathered their words. Hillel, patient. Shammai, strict. Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai, who rebuilt after the Temple fell. Rabbi Akiva. And Rabbi Meir, a name the Talmud reads as one who gives light. In tractate Eruvin it says that wasn't even his given name: he was called Meir because he lit up the eyes of the sages in the law. Now a surprise. In tractate Sanhedrin, the Talmud says a teaching in the Mishnah with no name on it follows Rabbi Meir, and adds: all of them follow Rabbi Akiva, his teacher. Even the unsigned lines have a teacher behind them, and a teacher behind him. A second surprise: the same word, tanna, also names a reciter in the house of study who had memorized great stores of teachings and could repeat them on request. And the Talmud, in tractate Sotah, teases them, in paraphrase: the tanna recites and doesn't know what he's saying. Repeating isn't understanding. The tannaim gave the teaching its words. Someone still had to explain them.
screen: `TANNA: ONE WHO REPEATS, AND TEACHES.` · `HILLEL TO RABBI JUDAH THE PRINCE.` · `MEIR: HE LIT UP THE SAGES' EYES.` · `UNSIGNED LINES STILL HAVE A TEACHER.` · then, large: `THE TEACHERS OF THE MISHNAH.`

segments.voice: Breathe in on Rabbi and out on Meir, the one who gave light, and let the name settle the way a tanna settled a teaching, by repeating it until it's yours. Then bring to mind someone who lit up a subject for you: a teacher, a parent, a coworker who explained what nobody else could. If you pray, you can give thanks for them.
Tanna. A teacher of the Mishnah, one of the sages from Hillel's time to Rabbi Judah the Prince, tied in the dictionary to repeating. Today's word.
Your line: the teachers of the mishnah. Their names stay attached to their words. That's day one thousand sixty-five.

howItsDone: When Jews study the Mishnah they quote it by its teachers, saying 'Rabbi Meir says' or 'the sages say', and it is a custom to repeat a teaching in the name of the one who said it.

chat.says: Who were the tannaim, and why does the Mishnah keep naming them?
options: The sages of the Mishnah, Hillel to Rabbi Judah; their names stay on what they taught.
Scribes who copied the Bible; the Mishnah names them to credit the handwriting.
Judges of the Temple court; the Mishnah names them to record each verdict.
chat.meaning: Tanna is tied to repeating. The tannaim are the sages of the Mishnah, and the book keeps each one's name with what he said.

notes: Tanna: the link to 'repeat, teach' is attributed to Jastrow's dictionary (cited). Please confirm the entry supports it.

Eruvin 13b paraphrased: Rabbi Meir's name was not Meir (the Talmud says it was Nehorai); he was called Meir because he enlightened the eyes of the sages in halakhah. 'Whose name means one who gives light' is the Talmud's own reading. Please confirm.
Sanhedrin 86a paraphrased (Rabbi Yochanan's statement): an unattributed mishnah is Rabbi Meir, and all follow Rabbi Akiva. Please confirm.
Sotah 22a paraphrased: the tanna recites and does not know what he says. The teaching that 'tanna' also names the academy reciter is stated; please confirm.
One-word sketches (Hillel patient, Shammai strict, Yochanan ben Zakkai rebuilt after the Temple fell) summarize earlier days; please confirm they are fair.
Range 'from the time of Hillel and Shammai down to Rabbi Judah the Prince' follows the outline; no dates given.
